Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: One sibling is preparing to try a new skateboard trick on a steep, uneven ramp.
Expectation2: Help out during difficult times or emergencies.
Situation2: A friend who has just started assembling furniture asks for a quick video call because the instructions are confusing.
Story: I stood at the edge of the skate park, watching my younger brother strap on his helmet, his eyes fixed on the steep, cracked ramp. He grinned at me, excitement and nerves mixing on his face. “Watch this, I’m finally going to land it,” he said, gripping his skateboard. My heart thudded with worry—he’d fallen hard last time, and I promised Mom I’d keep an eye on him. Just as he set his board down, my phone buzzed. It was Mia, my best friend. Her message popped up: “Can you video call? I’m stuck with this stupid bookshelf and about to lose it.” I could picture her surrounded by planks and screws, frustration mounting. She’d helped me through so much, and I knew she needed me now. But my brother was already rolling toward the ramp, and I felt torn in two—should I rush to Mia’s rescue or stay and make sure my brother didn’t get hurt? My hands shook as I hovered over my phone, caught between the two people who needed me most.
